summary: Phase I-4a of the immutable Nex Core plan: the pool rollout coordinator, in Core, tested with fake peers only. The pool master keeps one durable rollout record (pool-update.json beside pool-peer.json, replicated as the optional authority-replica section update_rollout) and its coordinator stages a release on every host in parallel, then updates one host at a time, members first and the master last, behind a quorum-margin gate, through the existing pool-maintenance command, with running_vms refuse or shutdown, an idempotent activate, a boot deadline, confirm, a same-host guest restart through normal start admission, and finalized_sequence. Controls pause, resume, abort and rollback_host; a promoted master finds an active rollout paused master_changed. The Controller relays one pool-update command per request and projects the master's record from inventory; it keeps nothing. The Controller appliance swap, the UI and the guide page are not in this slice.

guide.reason: No operator workflow can be walked through yet: the rollout is reachable only through the host-local and Controller APIs, there is no UI, and no lab (the project owner's resource cap rules out a three-host nested lab) exercised it. A guide page would claim unverified steps, so update-a-pool.md is deferred with the Controller UI and the lab walkthrough, and docs/qa/image/phase4-rollout.md records that it is open.

api.reason: New host-local master routes GET/POST /api/local/v1/pool/updates*, Controller routes GET /api/v1/pools/{id}/updates and POST …/updates/check, …/updates/rollouts and …/rollouts/{rollout_id}/control, peer routes POST /api/v1/pool/updates/step, GET …/status and GET …/blobs/{sha256}, the managed command pool-update (PoolCommand actions update-rollout and update-control, additive PoolCommand.update), the capability pool-update-rollout-v1, additive Inventory.managed.update_rollout (withheld until image-update-v1 is acknowledged) and the authority-replica section update_rollout (declared only while a record exists). Refusals carry a stable code; every mutation is idempotent on its request_id or step_id; the Controller answers 409 unless the master and every member advertise the capability.

roadmap.reason: Phase I-4 of a proposed, not yet authorized plan; development work validated by automated fake-peer tests only, no published milestone changed (the Phase 8 Rolling updates row is updated when a lab walkthrough passes).

state.reason: The pool master's Core owns and runs the rollout and keeps its only record; the Controller only asks (one durable pool-update command per request) and shows what the master reports, so deleting and reinstalling it loses nothing.
state.record: The pool master's pool-update.json in its agent store (beside pool-peer.json), replicated to members as the signed authority-replica section update_rollout, plus each host's own /var/lib/nex/image/state.json; a fresh Controller reads it back from the master's Inventory.managed.update_rollout once it acknowledges image-update-v1. The Controller keeps only the operations row it keeps for every host command.

verification.method: Go tests with fake peers and a fake host engine, no VM and no container: go test of ./internal/protocol ./internal/nexupdate/... ./internal/localcore ./internal/controller ./internal/agent; mutation checks on the quorum gate and the maintenance release; scripts/generate_api.py --check and tests/test_api_contract.py. See the QA record for what was and was not run.
